fields.v: Jiang, J., Zheng, S., Vidra, N., Setty, S. (2026). Beyond Pass@k: Measuring Reliability and Security of Agentic Code Generation. arXiv:2608.14711v1 [cs.AI], 11 Aug 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2608.14711v1 [cs.AI]; mentions 'the conference's policy' on generative AI but names no venue
Academia: Cornell University (Jiang, Zheng), Stevens Institute of Technology (Setty); industry: Anote.Ai (Vidra)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Evaluates — argues that test-case-based pass@k misapplies the Chen et al. estimator and proposes reliability@k (n = independent rollouts) and security-adjusted reliability@k within the CodeBench framework; tested on a synthetic rollout benchmark, a live-API run with three agent profiles and a 5-task SWE-bench Verified pilot with Claude Code

No SDD approach. Agent profiles: synthetic profiles 'agent-x', 'claude-code', 'codex' (H1-H3, not real systems); live-API wrappers (H4): agent-x and claude-code = claude-sonnet-4-6 with different system-prompt identities, codex = gpt-4o; SWE-bench pilot: Claude Code CLI v2.1.185 (headless, acceptEdits mode, model not stated)
N/A (no specification artefacts; tasks have a natural-language description, reference solution and test file)
N/A (no development flow prescribed)
None (automated runs)
N/A (no approach exercised; metrics evaluated)
Not classifiable (no specification approach); authors do not use SDD terms
New code for small algorithmic/data-structure problems (synthetic benchmark and live-API run, incl. 5 security-sensitive tasks); existing code base for the SWE-bench Verified pilot (astropy issues)

Synthetic: 10 tasks (3 easy, 3 medium, 4 hard) x 3 profiles x 8 rollouts = 240 synthetic results; live API: 10 tasks x 3 agents x 8 rollouts = 240 generations; pilot: 5 SWE-bench Verified instances from astropy/astropy (4 medium, 1 hard), one attempt each
General algorithmic programming (Python) and one scientific Python library (astropy) in the pilot
N/A (no human participants)
Defined but no values reported: cost-adjusted score = pass_rate / log(1 + cost_usd); tool efficiency = max(0, 1 - tool_calls/20)

Pass rate (tests passed / total), regression rate, test-case-based pass@k (criticised), reliability@k (Chen et al. estimator with n = independent rollouts, c = fully passing rollouts, pass_rate >= 0.95 in the synthetic setting), single-rollout proxy = pass_rate x (1 - regression_rate) x tool_efficiency; pilot: strict resolve rate (reliability@1), FAIL_TO_PASS / PASS_TO_PASS counts

Security score: heuristic scanner for seven high-severity patterns (eval, exec, os.system, subprocess shell=True, pickle.load, yaml.load without Loader, __import__), each -1/7; security-adjusted reliability@k counts rollouts passing all tests with security score >= 0.80
None
Score inflation (pass@5 minus reliability@5); Spearman correlation of proxy vs reliability@5; Kendall tau between rankings with and without the security adjustment

Automatic: synthetic generator make_rollout_benchmark (seed 42, latent skill ~ U[0.30, 1.0], truncated Gaussian per rollout); task-specific unit tests and the heuristic scanner for live-API generations; official SWE-bench harness in Docker for the pilot; leakage checks on agent inputs

Success criterion per rollout: passes all unit tests (synthetic: pass_rate >= 0.95); secure if scanner score >= 0.80; per task in the pilot: resolved by the official harness. No criterion stated by the authors for judging a configuration. (1) Synthetic profiles (not real systems; H2): agent-x pass@5 0.975 vs reliability@5 0.125; 'claude-code' 0.965 vs 0.000; 'codex' 0.959 vs 0.000. Verdicts: N/A (synthetic). (2) Live API, 'agent-x' wrapper + claude-sonnet-4-6 (H4): reliability@5 0.988, security-adjusted 0.988. Quality verdict: no criterion stated by the authors; cost not measured. (3) Live API, 'claude-code' wrapper + claude-sonnet-4-6: 0.793 / 0.793. Quality verdict: no criterion stated by the authors; cost not measured. (4) Live API, 'codex' wrapper + gpt-4o: 1.000 / 1.000. Quality verdict: no criterion stated by the authors; cost not measured. (5) Claude Code CLI v2.1.185 (acceptEdits, model not stated) on 5 SWE-bench Verified astropy tasks, one attempt: 1/5 resolved (reliability@1 0.20), macro hidden-test pass rate 0.8049, macro regression rate 0.1539; two near-misses, two regressive attempts (5 and 7 broken tests). Quality verdict: no criterion stated by the authors; cost not measured

Metric comparison (test-case-based pass@5 vs reliability@5) on synthetic data with 8 rollouts per (task, agent); proxy vs reliability@5 over 30 pairs with a pre-specified surrogate threshold rho >= 0.70; H4: three live-API agent profiles on a fixed 10-task set (5 algorithmic, 5 security-sensitive), 8 independent generations each, rank change threshold tau < 0.60; pilot: single agent, one attempt per task, no baseline. Held constant: task set and seed; agent-x and claude-code differ only by system-prompt identity. Acceptance: unit tests; official SWE-bench harness. Human intervention: none

H1 confirmed: identical 0.40 pass rates give pass@5 0.9762 vs 1.0000 by test-suite size. H2 confirmed: mean inflation 0.924 (0.85-0.97); ranking preserved (agent-x > claude-code > codex). H3 confirmed: proxy vs reliability@5 Spearman rho = 0.417 (p = 0.0218) < 0.70. H4 not confirmed: security adjustment changed no score or ranking (codex 1.000 > agent-x 0.988 > claude-code 0.793; Kendall tau = 1.000, p = 0.333); same model differs by 0.195 by system-prompt identity alone. Pilot: strict resolution 0.20 vs macro hidden-test pass 0.80

reliability@k distinguished synthetic profiles in absolute level but did not change rankings; security adjustment did not distinguish agents (under-powered: n = 3 agents, lenient threshold, half the tasks security-sensitive). Repeatable by seed (synthetic). Limitations stated: synthetic data, small agent pool, single unswept security threshold, scanner coverage, pilot of 5 tasks with one attempt and no self-testing

Synthetic, controlled data, not a production benchmark; H4 with three agents has minimal power; security threshold (>= 0.80) lenient and not swept; vulnerability-injection procedure may not cover real vulnerability classes (supply chain, business logic); SWE-bench pilot 5 tasks, one repository, one agent, one attempt, acceptEdits prevented running tests; proxy may misestimate reliability. Future work: validate against real vulnerability corpora, larger agent pool, threshold sweep, multi-attempt multi-repository SWE-bench runs for reliability@k with k > 1

No data or replication package link (functions such as make_rollout_benchmark named, code not released in the text). Hypothesis thresholds (inflation > 0.50, rho >= 0.70, tau < 0.60) called pre-specified, no registration. Programming language: Python. Inconsistencies: abstract gives reported scores 0.96-0.98 while the text says 0.96-0.97 (Table 1: 0.959-0.975); the claim that 'current implementations' and 'the field' misapply pass@k is supported only by the authors' own CodeBench implementation (p. 12); limitations mention a 'synthetic vulnerability-injection procedure' for security-labelled test cases that the setup does not describe; synthetic profiles are labelled 'claude-code' and 'codex' although they are not those systems, and the H4 'codex' profile is gpt-4o via API, not the Codex agent. Generative AI used to draft text and scripts (disclosed). Cost-adjusted score defined but not reported
Yes (1): two failures identified and hypotheses H1-H4 stated

Partly (0.5): claude-sonnet-4-6, gpt-4o and Claude Code CLI v2.1.185 named; gpt-4o snapshot, pilot model and wrapper details not stated; H1-H3 agents are synthetic
Partly (0.5): 10 tasks listed and pilot instances named, but the task set and tests are not made available
Yes (1): task-specific unit tests for live-API rollouts and the official SWE-bench harness for the pilot
Partly (0.5): quality and security metrics defined; cost-adjusted score defined but no cost values reported
Partly (0.5): three agent profiles on the same tasks in H4, but the pilot has a single agent and no baseline; H1-H3 compare metrics on synthetic data
Partly (0.5): 8 rollouts per pair, Spearman and Kendall tests; pilot one attempt; H4 test has minimal power
Partly (0.5): H4 non-confirmation and pilot scope reported honestly, but the claim that current benchmarks misapply pass@k rests only on the authors' own implementation and synthetic data

rev.why: Negative and limited results are reported honestly (H4 not confirmed, pilot scoped, Limitations stress synthetic data), which supports Yes; but the abstract and introduction claim that 'current implementations' and 'the field' misapply pass@k, while the evidence is only the authors' own CodeBench implementation and synthetic data (p. 12), which supports Partly

Negative and limited results are reported honestly (H4 not confirmed, pilot scoped, Limitations stress synthetic data), which supports Yes; but the abstract and introduction claim that 'current implementations' and 'the field' misapply pass@k, while the evidence is only the authors' own CodeBench implementation and synthetic data (p. 12), which supports Partly

fields.warn: O artigo relata bem o H4 falhado e o âmbito do piloto, mas afirma que 'a área' usa mal o pass@k com base só na sua própria implementação (p. 12). Decide entre Partly e Yes.
